sentences[1].why: dies- points at one: der-ending again — Dieser (or just Der).

sentences[3].why: Pointing at the die-word: Diese Tasche — dies- + e.
sentences[4].why: das Buch → Welches — the das-ending -es; das-words don't change in the accusative.

sentences[6].why: mit takes the dative: masculine -em — meinem Bruder.
sentences[9].why: mit + dative: der Bus → welchem — the dative endings are -m/-r/-m/-n.
sentences[10].why: in + position = dative: das Haus → diesem — das-words take -em there.

help.intro: Three small article-words round off the case system so far. welch-? asks 'which?' and dies- answers 'this' — and both take the endings of der/die/das in every case: welcher / dieser (der), welche / diese (die), welches / dieses (das), welchen / diesen (accusative masculine), welchem / diesem and welcher / dieser (dative). In conversation the plain article does the same job: Welchen Film? – Den hier. The third piece is the possessives in the dative — meinem Bruder, meiner Schwester, meinen Eltern — which follow the ein-word pattern: -em, -er, -em, -en. After mit, bei, von, zu and every dative verb, that is the ending you need.
help.tips[0].title: welch- and dies- take der-endings
help.tips[0].text: Nominative: welcher / welche / welches. Accusative: welchen (masculine only changes). Dative: welchem / welcher / welchem. Same for dieser, diese, dieses, diesen, diesem.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: Which train goes to Cologne? – This one.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: Which coat are you taking? – This one.
help.tips[0].check.why: The pullover is the object of kaufst, so masculine accusative: welchen, like den.
help.tips[1].title: Der da, die hier — pointing with the article
help.tips[1].text: Spoken German points with the bare article: Welche Tasche? – Die da. Welches Buch? – Das hier. It is exactly as correct as dieser.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: Which cake would you like? – The one with chocolate.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: Which dress do you like? – This one.
help.tips[1].check.q: Welchen Rock nimmst du? – ____ hier. (der Rock)
help.tips[1].check.why: The bare article answers in the same case as the question: Welchen Rock? – Den hier, masculine accusative.
help.tips[2].title: Possessives in the dative: -em, -er, -em, -en
help.tips[2].text: mit meinem Bruder, mit meiner Schwester, mit meinem Kind, mit meinen Eltern. dein, sein, ihr, unser, euer, Ihr do the same: bei seiner Oma, von ihrem Chef, zu unseren Freunden.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: I live with my parents and go to school with my brother.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: The present is from our neighbours.
help.tips[2].trap: 'mit meine Schwester' keeps the nominative. After mit the possessive needs its dative ending: meiner.
help.tips[2].check.q: Am Wochenende fahre ich mit ____ Freundin nach Hamburg. (die Freundin)
help.tips[2].check.why: mit takes the dative, and the feminine dative ending is -er: meiner.
help.tips[3].title: The dative endings are always -m / -r / -m / -n
help.tips[3].text: dem, der, dem, den · einem, einer, einem · meinem, meiner, meinem, meinen · welchem, welcher, welchem, welchen. Different words, same four endings.
help.tips[3].examples[0].en: by this bus, in this city, from which country
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: Which train are you taking? – This one.
help.tips[3].check.why: aus takes the dative, and feminine dative ends in -r, just like der: welcher.
help.remember[1]: Dative is m–r–m–n on every article word.
help.context.en: Which film are we watching today? – This one, the new one. – And which bus are we taking? – The number ten, it stops outside the cinema. – Is your sister coming? – Yes, I'm going with my sister and her boyfriend. We're meeting at my parents'.
help.mistakes[2].why: Dative plural: meinen (+ -n on the noun where possible).
help.hook: Point at exactly what you mean — Welchen? Diesen hier! — and say who you're with: mit meinem Bruder, bei meiner Schwester.
